retention.stated: Independent disks and persistent state; snapshots go to S3 every few minutes; volume storage bills for each hour the volume exists even while the attached Sailbox sleeps.

record.interface_detail: HTTPS API at sailbox-api.sailresearch.com, SDKs (Python, TypeScript), the sail CLI and SSH to devboxes
record.tooling: the `sail` CLI, the Python SDK (`import sail`) and the TypeScript SDK `@sailresearch/sdk`, all built on the public HTTPS API
record.chaining: A Sailbox is a full VM that never has to be torn down: the sleeping state is free, so a long-horizon agent keeps its filesystem, packages and running processes across days and pays only for the seconds it works. Pairing the USD 5 monthly credit with a sleeping box converts the credit into about 39 hours of active compute a month, which is an hour and a quarter a day.

limits.value: USD 0.015 per active vCPU-hour and USD 0.008 per active GB-hour; a free-plan creation fee of USD 0.005 to USD 0.012

record.limits_note: The smallest Sailbox holds 16 GiB of RAM, and RAM bills whether or not it is touched, so the floor is USD 0.128 per hour before a single vCPU-second is used; USD 5 of monthly credit buys about 39 hours of that.
record.binding_note: Active-CPU metering is the wall in both directions: a busy box costs USD 16.79 a month, and the disk keeps billing even while the box sleeps.

identity_cost.detail: The first-party marketing page states '$5 in free credits every month when you attach a payment method'; card type and any hold are unverified.

record.reliability_note: In-flight work survives pause and resume, and open connections survive pauses up to 10 minutes; the runtime column on the marketing page says Unlimited.

record.notes: Arithmetic at 1 vCPU / 1 GiB fully active for 730 h: 0.015 x 730 = USD 10.95 + 0.008 x 730 = USD 5.84 = USD 16.79. The metering is on ACTIVE CPU, so a mostly idle box is cheaper: at 5% average CPU the compute line is USD 0.55 and the memory line USD 5.84, which is USD 6.39 and still over the line because memory is charged while the box runs. This is the provider whose pricing model most rewards idling, and it still cannot reach USD 5 at 1 GiB. The 'no runtime limits' claim is the vendor's own and was not tested.

extras.price_arithmetic: (0.015 + 0.008) = USD 0.023/hour at full activity x 730 h = USD 16.79; x 300 h = USD 6.90. At 5% average CPU the compute line falls to USD 0.55 and the total to USD 6.39. Volume storage adds 0.000411/GiB-hour = USD 0.30/GiB-month.
